utterances.text: All right. On the basis of what did you conclude that even if some criminals did appear in (redacted), that it was that soldier who called them? One of these who had been with you before that. On the basis of what did you conclude that he was the one who called them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K24
utterances.text: I saw this. I saw them leaving us, and then they came back with these criminals together with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did that soldier go, or rather, these three soldiers who escorted you to (redacted)? Did they return to their unit, or did they stay with these criminals too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K24
utterances.text: They went back to (redacted). They left us together with the criminals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That actually means that they were not criminals but they were connected to criminals. Would that approximately be the most correct way of putting it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K24
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain this at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that some people misbehaved towards women who were with you, you are actually referring to these criminals, aren't you? You're referring to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K24
utterances.text: Yes, criminals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as I can see from your statement, you did not see them rape any person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K24
utterances.text: It was me myself that they insulted and offended. I didn't see any of the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you see here on page 7 of your statement, in the last paragraph, you say before that: "All of those who were from (redacted) returned to (redacted). We returned to (redacted)when it got dark. They put us into the -- they put us into the shed of a house that was about 300 metres away, where they kept us locked. The house had been burned. I don't know who it belonged to. They, the three soldiers, left us there alone, saying, Nothing is going to happen to you. Do not be scared. They brought us bread, a candle, (redacted), and they said, Tomorrow we are going to find the girls and the women. They told us not to go out because otherwise we would be in danger because of the paramilitaries." "The paramilitaries" was probably written by the person who actually wrote the statement. I imagine that you yourself were using Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the term "criminals"; is that right? And you say further on: "They were showing --" I hear the interpretation into Albanian finishing only now. So actually, what it says here, "paramilitaries," that is what you have been calling "criminals," right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K24
utterances.text: Yes, criminals.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Just referring to the witness, she has not been given an opportunity to respond to the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: She's got as far as the criminals. Yes, what's the next question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, precisely, that's what I wanted to establish, that these were criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So: "They brought us bread, a candle, (redacted), et cetera. They told us not to go out because otherwise we would be in danger of the criminals," as you put it, it says "paramilitaries" here. And then further on, it says, "They were showing that they were trying to protect us. We stayed in that house for ten days without a guard. The three soldiers went back to (Redacted), but in the next-door house were other Yugoslav army soldiers that said to us, Whatever you need, just call us. After seven days, Mirdita came there and she stayed with us for three days," et cetera, et cetera. "During those seven days, they (the soldiers) came very often. They provoked us. They asked us for money." So how did that change all of a sudden? First they did all of this for you and they said, "Just call us if you need anything," and then they started to provoke you, ask for money, and one of them even pointed a gun at your head. What happened? You say that this Mirdita came seven days later and then something changed. What happened? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K24
utterances.text: When Mirdita came, she was in agreement with them, and we didn't see them any more. We only communicated through Mirdita.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on the basis of what I've just quoted to you, Mrs. K24, on the basis of that, can it be seen that you yourself wrote that the soldiers brought you there, left you there, and that after that, for several days other soldiers in the neighbourhood took care of you and none of those three brought in any criminals? You say here: "Three soldiers left us there on our own and said, Nothing is going to happen to you. Do not be scared." And then they brought all these things to you and then you say that you stayed there without a guard for ten days in that house. Those soldiers went back to (Redacted) and other Yugoslav army soldiers said to you, "Whatever you need, just call us."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's now past quarter to and we have to adjourn. Is there a question you want to ask?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I don't want to maltreat this witness. I don't want to keep her until tomorrow for the end. I have just one more question, then I'll finish immediately, because I think that she has suffered enough, and I really don't want to keep her here overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell me one more thing, please. You and Mirdita, as you've described this here, you were taken to the hospital in (redacted) by the Serbs. That is on page 03031924. Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K24
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The Yugoslav army took us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, that was a very appropriate gesture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wladimiroff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Romano.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Just one question and I'll be very brief. Re-examined by Ms. Romano:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you referred to the three men, the criminals, the men that the soldiers called, were they wearing any -- how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K24
utterances.text: They had a uniform, light blue. It was a light colour with a tiger sign on the arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's just that I have -- you referred to copies, separate copies of the photos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: I just remind also that the description of the photos and referred by the witness are in the addendum of the bis package. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K24, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are now free to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now. Nine o'clock tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
